steps.label: Totipotency
steps.margin_note: Definition plus the reason it is possible.
lines: TOTIPOTENCY is the ability of a single cell to
Every living plant cell carries the whole genome,
so in principle any of them can do it.
steps.why: Each cell carries a complete copy of the genome, so nothing is missing that would stop it rebuilding the whole organism.
common_mistakes: Saying totipotency means a cell can divide. It means it can become a WHOLE PLANT.
Saying only meristem cells are totipotent. Any living plant cell is, in principle.

steps.label: Explant
steps.margin_note: Definition with sterile conditions and the medium, plus examples.

lines.text: Totipotency is the property; the explant is

lines: An EXPLANT is any part of a plant that is taken
out and grown in a test tube, under STERILE
conditions, in a special NUTRIENT MEDIUM, to
Examples: a piece of root, stem, leaf, or a shoot
steps.why: The explant is only useful because its cells are totipotent, which is why the two terms are always defined together.
common_mistakes: Saying an explant is a whole plant. It is a small PIECE cut from a plant — a bit of root, stem, leaf or a shoot tip — grown in a sterile nutrient medium.
Leaving out the sterile conditions. They are part of the definition.
steps.memory_tip: Totipotency is why it works; the explant is what you start with.
